topics.title: Stop rereading. Try this study trick instead 📚 #Shorts
topics.hook: Rereading your notes can feel productive, but try testing your memory instead.
steps: Read one small section, then close your notes.
Write down everything you can remember without looking.
Check your notes and fill in the gaps you missed.
topics.takeaway: Make your brain retrieve the answer. That is active recall.
topics.description: A practical introduction to active recall: retrieve information from memory, check your gaps, and repeat.

topics.title: Can't focus? Try the 25-minute reset ⏱️ #Shorts
topics.hook: If starting feels impossible, make the study session smaller.
steps: Choose one task you can work on for 25 minutes.
Put your phone away and close unrelated tabs.
Take a five-minute break when the timer ends.
topics.takeaway: One focused sprint is better than waiting for perfect motivation.
topics.description: Use a simple Pomodoro-style focus sprint to get started and build momentum.

topics.title: The secret to remembering more: space it out 🧠 #Shorts
topics.hook: Want to remember what you study next week? Don't leave all the revision until tonight.
steps: Review a new idea soon after you first learn it.
Test yourself again after a day or two.
Return to it later in the week, then again after a longer gap.
topics.takeaway: Short reviews spread over time can make recall stronger than one big cram session.
topics.description: A quick introduction to spaced practice and why revisiting material over time helps learning.

topics.title: Your to-do list is too big. Do this first ✨ #Shorts
topics.hook: A huge assignment feels less scary when you stop treating it as one task.
steps: Write the final thing you need to hand in.
Split it into three small actions you can actually start.
Choose the first action and work on it for ten minutes.
topics.takeaway: Make the next step obvious, small and easy to begin.
topics.description: A simple way to break a big assignment into smaller, more manageable actions.

topics.title: If you can teach it simply, you understand it 🎓 #Shorts
topics.hook: Here's a quick way to check whether a topic really makes sense to you.
steps: Pick one concept from your notes.
Explain it out loud as if teaching a younger student.
Notice where you get stuck, then revisit only that part.
topics.takeaway: Explaining an idea reveals gaps that highlighting can hide.
topics.description: Use the teach-back technique to check your understanding and find knowledge gaps.

topics.title: Study breaks are not wasted time 🌿 #Shorts
topics.hook: Taking a break is part of a good study plan, not a failure of discipline.
steps: Step away from your desk for a few minutes.
Stretch, drink water or look away from your screen.
Decide on the one task you'll return to next.
topics.takeaway: A real break helps you reset your attention before the next session.
topics.description: Build short, intentional breaks into your study routine to reset between focus sessions.

topics.title: Exam coming up? Start with this 3-step plan 📝 #Shorts
topics.hook: When exams are close, don't just reread everything from page one.
steps: List the topics and mark the ones you find hardest.
Spend your first revision block on one difficult topic.
Do practice questions and review every mistake.
topics.takeaway: Use practice to find what needs work, then focus your revision there.
topics.description: A practical three-step approach to organising revision before an exam.
